domain_setting: A friendly fitness studio, neighborhood gym and quiet recovery space. The tone is encouraging, non-competitive and non-judgmental.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use a 304×192 scene with a gym floor, exercise mat, small bench, or recovery-room cue as appropriate.
Keep people varied and comfortably dressed; show capable movement without idealized body shapes or weight judgments.
Use thick volumetric limbs and clear poses; avoid stick figures and distinguish similar exercise actions by their body position and tool.
Show gym machines with recognizable moving parts and handles; keep the room setting simple so the target equipment stays central.
Keep breathing, meditation, stress, sleep and therapy scenes calm and non-clinical; avoid dramatic distress or medical outcomes.
Use simple pictorial measurement cues for heart rate without digits, and use consent-respecting, non-graphic wellness scenes.

polysemy_resolution_table.aerobics: Group rhythmic exercise with coordinated arm movement; not an abstract science term.
polysemy_resolution_table.boot camp: A challenging group fitness class with an instructor and exercise stations; not military recruitment or new-recruit training.
polysemy_resolution_table.cardio: Sustained cardiovascular exercise such as brisk cycling or running, with a gentle raised heart-rate cue; not a heart procedure.
polysemy_resolution_table.circuit training: A sequence of several exercise stations and actions; distinguish from one exercise class.
polysemy_resolution_table.cool down: Gentle post-exercise movement and breathing; not lowering room temperature.
polysemy_resolution_table.exercise: Physical activity in a clear movement pose; distinguish from a formal class and from workout as a session.
polysemy_resolution_table.exercise class: A small group following an instructor through a movement routine.
polysemy_resolution_table.fitness: Physical conditioning and capability; not suitability or appropriateness.
polysemy_resolution_table.jog: A relaxed running gait; not nudging an object.
polysemy_resolution_table.jump rope: The action of jumping over a turning rope; distinguish from the skipping rope as equipment.
polysemy_resolution_table.keep fit: A repeated routine combining exercise and activity; not a single exercise pose.
polysemy_resolution_table.pilates: Controlled floor-based core exercise on a mat; distinguish from yoga poses.
polysemy_resolution_table.push-up / press-up (often uk): A complete body held straight while lowering and pushing up from the floor.
polysemy_resolution_table.run: A faster running stride with a lifted leg and arm swing; distinguish from jogging and walking.
polysemy_resolution_table.sit-up: A person rising from lying to seated with knees bent; not a generic abdominal pose.
polysemy_resolution_table.skip: The hopping running gait; not skipping rope or a missing item.
polysemy_resolution_table.squat: A person bending knees and hips into a low position while keeping balance.
polysemy_resolution_table.stretch: An extended limb or torso reaching through a deliberate muscle stretch.
polysemy_resolution_table.train: A person coaching or practicing exercise; not a rail vehicle.
polysemy_resolution_table.warm up: Gentle preparatory movement before exercise; not heating equipment.
polysemy_resolution_table.walk: A normal walking stride with one foot in contact with the floor; distinguish from running.
polysemy_resolution_table.workout: A complete planned exercise session with more than one activity or piece of equipment.
polysemy_resolution_table.yoga: A controlled yoga balance or seated pose on a mat; not generic stretching or meditation.
polysemy_resolution_table.changing room: A private place to change clothes, shown with a bench and privacy stalls; distinguish from locker storage.
polysemy_resolution_table.elliptical / cross-trainer: A cardio machine with two foot pedals moving on an oval path and paired hand poles.
polysemy_resolution_table.exercise bike: A stationary bicycle used for indoor exercise; distinguish from an outdoor bicycle.
polysemy_resolution_table.exercise mat: A rolled or flat cushioned mat used for floor exercise; not a yoga pose.
polysemy_resolution_table.gym: An indoor fitness facility with exercise equipment; not school gymnastics.
polysemy_resolution_table.locker room: A shared changing area with benches and lockers; distinguish from one private changing room.
polysemy_resolution_table.lockers: A row of storage compartments for bags and clothing; not a whole locker room.
polysemy_resolution_table.rowing machine: Indoor exercise equipment with a sliding seat, handle and foot rests; not a boat.
polysemy_resolution_table.skipping rope: The rope as a handled exercise tool; distinguish from the person jumping over it.
polysemy_resolution_table.treadmill: An indoor running machine with a moving belt and front handrail; not a manual foot-powered wheel.
polysemy_resolution_table.acupuncture: A calm practitioner placing a few fine needles on a clothed, consenting client; no blood or distress.
polysemy_resolution_table.aromatherapy: Relaxation with a small essential-oil diffuser and gentle scent swirls; not a cure.
polysemy_resolution_table.chill out: A person reclining comfortably in a relaxed setting; not cooling down after exercise.
polysemy_resolution_table.counseling: A supportive conversation between a professional and a client in a private calm room; not physical therapy.
polysemy_resolution_table.deep breathing: A person sitting comfortably with slow, expanded breathing cues; not hyperventilation.
polysemy_resolution_table.hot tub: A small warm-water tub with gentle bubbles; distinguish from a swimming pool.
polysemy_resolution_table.massage: A trained practitioner using hands to massage a clothed or draped client’s shoulders; respectful and non-graphic.
polysemy_resolution_table.meditate: A person quietly focused in a seated mindfulness pose; not merely thinking through a problem.
polysemy_resolution_table.reflexology: A practitioner gently pressing a client’s foot; keep the scene clean, consensual and non-clinical.
polysemy_resolution_table.relax: A person visibly easing tension with shoulders lowered and a calm pose; not an exercise cool down.
polysemy_resolution_table.sauna: A dry-heat wooden room with a bench; distinguish from the humid steam room.
polysemy_resolution_table.sleep well: A restful sleeper with a calm bed scene and subtle restful cues; emphasize quality of sleep.
polysemy_resolution_table.spa: A wellness setting with a pool or treatment area; distinguish from one sauna, massage or hot tub.
polysemy_resolution_table.steam room: A tiled humid room with visible soft vapor; distinguish from the dry wooden sauna.
polysemy_resolution_table.sleep: A person asleep in bed with closed eyes and night setting; distinguish from advice to sleep well.
polysemy_resolution_table.stress: A person with tense shoulders and a few visual tension cues, kept mild and empathetic.
polysemy_resolution_table.wellness: A broad balance of movement, rest and calm; avoid implying a cure or one ideal body.
polysemy_resolution_table.heart rate: A pulse being checked at the wrist with a simple heart-wave cue and no numbers.
polysemy_resolution_table.personal trainer: A fitness coach guiding one client through a safe exercise with encouraging body language.
polysemy_resolution_table.strength: Physical ability shown through a controlled lift or stable carry; avoid body-size stereotypes.

existing_asset_triage.lesson_71: Scanned all existing SVGs for exact same-term keys across the full library. No exact candidates were found for the 53 Chapter 71 terms; all scenes will be drawn in the fitness and well-being context.

glossary_context_notes: Japanese glosses for train, fitness, jog, gym and meditate point to unrelated meanings; lesson grouping resolves them to exercise, conditioning, running, a fitness facility and mindfulness.
Keep paired motions distinct: walk/jog/run/skip, warm up/cool down, jump rope/skipping rope, pilates/yoga, changing room/locker room, sauna/steam room, sleep/sleep well, and exercise/workout/fitness.
Avoid medicalized or coercive wellness imagery; portray physical activity and recovery as approachable choices.
